::: {#hero-heading}
In 1971, Wadlo Tobler and S. Wineburg published a very short, two-page article in the journal *Nature* in which they attempted to pinpoint the locations of Hittite cities through the analysis of cuneiform tablets @tobler1971. A year earlier, he had formulated—albeit to general indifference—his famous first law of geography: “Everything is related to everything else, but nearby things are more related than distant things” @tobler1970. While the 1970 article on the first law of geography would go on to achieve resounding success over time (15,129 citations in Google Scholar as of June 2026), the second did not enjoy such lasting impact (141 citations), even though its importance is undoubtedly at least equal.

The aim of the Sirius project is to revisit Tobler’s reasoning regarding the Hittite tablets by applying it to news articles circulating worldwide between 2013 and 2020 in order to deduce a political geometry of our contemporary world.
:::
